title: roman-to-numeral
statement: The roman package exposes is_roman_numeral (already implemented) and a stub to_roman(n). Implement to_roman(n) so that it converts an integer n in the range 1..3999 inclusive to its standard Roman numeral string using subtractive notation (4='IV', 9='IX', 40='XL', 90='XC', 400='CD', 900='CM'). Return a str. Raise ValueError when n is an int outside 1..3999. Raise TypeError when n is not an int (for example '5', 5.0, None, [1]); numeric strings and integral floats are not coerced. Type discipline is by value: an instance of an int subclass (for example an IntEnum member or `class PlainInt(int)`) is accepted and converted exactly like the int with the same value, including the range check. Int subclasses that override arithmetic or comparison operators are out of scope: their behaviour is unspecified and tests must not depend on it. bool is a subclass of int; rejecting True and False with TypeError is permitted but not required, and tests must not depend on either choice. Do not change is_roman_numeral or the tests.
acceptance_criteria: ValueError for ints outside 1..3999 (0, -1, 4000), including int subclass instances with such values
An int subclass instance with a value in range (for example an IntEnum member or PlainInt(49)) converts like the equal int: PlainInt(49) -> 'XLIX'
Unspecified, not to be tested: int subclasses that override arithmetic or comparison operators; whether bool is rejected
contract_resolution: 2026-10-17: the 17 Oct Codex dry run held a correct candidate on three breaker tests that drove to_roman through int subclasses with overridden __floordiv__/__mod__/__ge__/__le__; the statement was silent on such subclasses and its bool clause was garbled. The requester resolved the gap: conversion is by integer value, operator-overriding subclasses are out of scope, bool handling is unspecified. Recorded in reports/attest-reliability-2026-10-17/.
